title: Relocate modules and split ownership
goal: Move the complete Scopes, Audit and DevTools slices into their module roots and split schema, installer, health and configuration ownership, keeping one decision/write path and all data intact.
context: Architecture phase C (revision 2, D7, D11, D12). Approximate size: L. FQCN changes follow the P2 upgrade map; durable data does not change. Complete slices include providers, config sections, health checks, commands, migrations, stubs and contract suites.

consumes: The P2 contracts and upgrade map
produces: modules/scopes, modules/audit and modules/devtools with explicit PSR-4 roots and single autoload ownership

Six-table StorageSchema create/drop and core health; Audit migration with fixed basename, adoption, non-destructive down() and per-storage generator; Audit health and retention without the authority lock
DevTools-owned onboarding, generators, stubs and scaffold section; owner-registered config sections
Concrete-source branches removed from decision/query semantics; any further read-coordinator restructuring gated by I21/I22
Activation-matrix fixtures and relocated consumer/generator fixtures
boundaries: No core→module, module↔module or module↔Filament references (allowlists empty)
No inactive-module I/O, service resolution or compulsory optional table
Physical-handle snapshots, bounded fenced re-reads and root-commit publication preserved

include: Module trees, composer autoload and provider metadata
StorageSchema, StorageHealth, doctor checks, migrations and storage/audit migration commands
AzGuardServiceProvider and module providers, console commands and stubs
exclude: Physical extraction into new Composer products
Feature expansion or relaxed exact-query semantics
Exposing internal database mechanisms as public SPI

pitfalls: Moving the plugin alone leaves schema/config/health/provider dependencies in core
Overlapping PSR-4 prefixes need an empty src/Scopes|Audit|DevTools to keep one owner
Audit adoption must verify full shape, including SQLite triggers, and change nothing on mismatch
Prune without the panel lock needs concurrent insert/prune runs on MySQL and MariaDB
Published copies of core migrations now build six tables; teardown must keep audit data

validation.procedure: Run the core-only fixture with module roots absent and every activation combination including two panels with different options; replay all persistence scenarios on populated 0.7.0 fixtures per driver; run parity, rollback/retry/event-id, physical-handle release, cache fingerprint, concurrent prune and archive consumer checks.
validation.expect: I2, I3, I5, I13, I15 and I16 green with empty allowlists; all P1/P2 checks stay green; zero grant, identity or audit-row rewrite.

deliverables: Final ownership/dependency map and module activation matrix
Separated module providers, config sections, schema, commands and stubs
Audit installation/adoption chain incl. named storages

sections.title: Mandatory design inputs
sections.text:
The detailing session for P3 reads these before authoring any item (`show` of this phase is the entry point; the list is mandatory):

```bash
P='python3 <task>/scripts/plan.py'; ID=2026.10.10-№1-AZGUARD-CORE-STABILIZATION
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section ownership
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section scope-boundary
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section operation-chains
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section persistence
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section invariants
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section risks
$P get $ID knowledge/target-structure            # all sections (the trees are the target)
$P get $ID knowledge/type-map            # all zones; rows with phase P3 are this phase's scope
$P get $ID knowledge/identities            # commands, config, resources, doctor
$P get $ID knowledge/upgrade-map            # all sections
$P get $ID knowledge/contracts            # audit, storage, config, scopes-plugin
$P get $ID D5
$P get $ID D7
$P get $ID D11
$P get $ID D12
$P get $ID D13
```

Rules for the detailed items:

- Each item lists in `reads` (with `section`, `required: true`) the reference sections it implements; a phase-bound document that no item reads is reported by `design-done` (`phase_documents_unread`) and must be resolved before the phase counts as detailed.
- Items cite their type-map rows by current FQCN in `scope.include`; an item may not move, rename or re-mark a type differently from `knowledge/type-map`.
- If `design-done` reports a pack over the 256 KB budget, move the binding of a reference document from the phase to the items that read it (`plan.py unlink … --kind applies_to`, `plan.py link …`) — never drop the read.
- After P3 the tree under each root equals `knowledge/target-structure`; I5 checks it against `artifacts/inventory/target-map.json` with `target_path`.

sections.title: Exit criterion
sections.text: The target boundaries exist in code, including every composition root, config section and resource owner. Core boots, checks and writes without module roots, and all supported paths agree on authority.
